decisions.location: Results: exact Fang original-specific inverse V1/LO comparison; Discussion central replication synthesis
decisions.quote:
Fang et al. (2008) extended Murray et al.’s (2002)
results by demonstrating that in addition to the clear
reduction of activation in V1, there was also a reversal
of this pattern in a region they labeled as LOC. We did
not ﬁnd a clear increase in the whole of LOC (LO and
pFs, see Methods, F(15, 150) ¼ 1.23, p ¼ 0.236, but

upon discussing this discrepancy with the original
authors (F. Fang, personal communication, August
17, 2012) it appears plausible that the region they
labeled LOC in fact only contained what we have
deﬁned as the more posterior shape selective region LO.
The increase in LO is not as large as that reported by
Fang et al. but it is still quite robust, F(15, 150) ¼ 3.96,
p , 0.001). It is also likely that the more anterior shape
selective region on the ventral surface that we have
labeled pFs corresponds to what Fang et al. labeled
temporal object areas (TOA). Although there is a
similar pattern of results in pFs to that found in LO
(see Figure 5) these are not signiﬁcant, F(15, 150) ¼
0.74, p ¼ 0.7, a pattern broadly consistent with the
results of Fang et al.
decisions.reason: For the now-bound empirical Fang2008target, the authors replicate V1/V2decreases and an opposite robust increase in posterior LO, with weak anterior pFs/TOA modulation and V3null broadly consistent with Fang. They explicitly call their parameter-matched result a replication in the Discussion. The initially discrepant whole-LOC label is discussed as a likely LO/pFs region-definition difference, rather than an author-declared original-specific empirical failure. No verified mask equality is asserted. The principal new finding challenges retinotopic specificity of feedback, which the current authors call a theoretical assumption; Fang measured predefined stimulus ROIs and did not establish an empirical off-stimulus null. Disconfirming that inferred assumption does not add a failed empirical finding to the replicated V1/LOpattern. Preserve raw mixed as a contrary opinion, but do not convert an unmeasured original off-stimulus comparison or smaller amplitude into empirical nonreplication. This is a material parent judgment under the empirical-target and author-synthesis rules.

decisions.quote:
All 13 participants completed three types of fMRI
runs: Diamond, Stimulus-Speciﬁc-Checkerboard, and
Large-Square-Wave-Grating, which will be described
below. Moreover, all the participants also completed

 Journal of Vision (2012) 12(11):12, 1–14

de-Wit, Kubilius, Wagemans, & Op de Beeck

Meridian-Mapping and Object-Versus-Scrambled-Object runs and a T1 weighted structural run (these data
were available from a previous experiment for six
participants, see Kubilius et al., 2011).
In the Diamond runs participants were presented
with 16 seconds of ﬁxation at the start of the run
followed by 403 seconds of the bistable moving
diamond / lines stimulus followed by a further 13
seconds of ﬁxation. Participants had to ﬁxate on a
small central dot during the entire run. The Diamond
stimulus consisted of four oriented lines that moved
such that they could be interpreted either as four lines
moving separately (local condition) or as one solid
(‘diamond’) shape moving horizontally behind three
invisible occluding bars (global condition; Figure 1).
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding classify type as 'replication'. De-Wit et al. (2012) collected new fMRI data from 13 newly tested participants at the University of Leuven (12 analyzed after excluding 1 participant lacking baseline fixation normalization; final ROI samples: 11 for V1 and LOC, 10 for V2, 9 for V3; edb96f4b87f5413a.txt chars 11727-13876, 17912-23532). Although Meridian-Mapping, Object-Versus-Scrambled-Object localizer, and T1 structural scans were available from a prior study (Kubilius et al., 2011) for 6 of the participants, all 13 participants completed new Diamond, Stimulus-Specific-Checkerboard, and Large-Square-Wave-Grating experimental fMRI runs testing the bistable diamond paradigm of Fang et al. (2008) and Murray et al. (2002, Experiment 3) in an independent sample.
